objective: Research India's electric mobility industry over the last six months. Identify significant competitor developments, product launches, manufacturing expansions, partnerships, investment activity, policy developments, procurement opportunities and emerging commercial opportunities. Prioritize original company announcements and official government sources. Separate verified facts from analysis and provide the sources supporting every finding.

result.executive_summary: India’s electric mobility sector has accelerated sharply over the last six months, driven by strong government programmes (PARIVARTAN, PM E‑DRIVE, PLI‑ACC), significant OEM commitments and rising private‑sector investment. Key OEMs (Tata Motors, Mahindra & Mahindra, TVS Motor, Ola Electric) have entered new MoUs, expanded manufacturing capacity and launched new models, while the government has allocated over ₹20 billion in incentives for EVs, charging infrastructure and battery‑cell production.
result.industry_overview: The EV ecosystem in India is transitioning from a nascent market to a mature manufacturing hub. EV registrations grew ~46‑fold since 2016, with two‑wheelers and three‑wheelers leading adoption. Domestic production now covers battery packs, motors, drivetrains, power electronics and charging equipment, supported by multiple policy levers (FAME‑II, PM E‑DRIVE, PLI‑Auto, PLI‑ACC).
market_trends: EV sales surged ~46 times since 2016 (Roads Reimagined, 2026)
Battery‑cell capacity under PLI‑ACC expected to reach ~95 GWh from private players (PLI ACC agreement, 2022)
OEMs are investing in gigafactories and dedicated EV platforms (Roads Reimagined, 2026)
company_developments: Tata Motors, Mahindra & Mahindra, TVS Motor and others signed MoUs under the PARIVARTAN scheme to supply cleaner trucks and buses in Delhi‑NCR (PARIVARTAN, 2026)
Ola Electric secured a PLI‑ACC agreement to develop ACC battery capacity contributing to the ~95 GWh private‑sector target (PLI ACC, 2022)
product_launches: Roads Reimagined notes the inauguration of Suzuki’s first global BEV ‘e VITARA’ in August 2025, signalling new model introductions by OEMs (Roads Reimagined, 2026)
manufacturing_expansion: PLI‑ACC agreement earmarks private‑sector capacity of ~95 GWh, with Ola Electric among the three firms receiving incentives to build large‑scale battery plants (PLI ACC, 2022)
OEMs such as Tata Motors, Mahindra, TVS are expanding capacity through gigafactory investments (Roads Reimagined, 2026)
partnerships_and_investment: PARIVARTAN MoUs bind 11 OEMs—including Tata Motors and Mahindra—to the Delhi‑NCR truck‑bus replacement programme (PARIVARTAN, 2026)
India’s EV ecosystem attracted > USD 1.4 billion in FY 2025, with OEMs securing ~USD 1.2 billion (Roads Reimagined, 2026)
policy_and_regulatory: PARIVARTAN scheme approved 3 June 2026, total outlay ₹9,585 crore for truck‑bus renewal (PARIVARTAN, 2026)
PM E‑DRIVE scheme outlay ₹10,900 crore; as of 22 July 2026 it has incentivised 2,322,878 EVs and allocated ₹2,000 crore for EV public‑charging stations (PM E‑DRIVE, 2026)
PLI‑ACC scheme budget ₹18,100 crore; aims for 50 GWh ACC capacity, with private‑sector target ~95 GWh (PLI ACC, 2022)
tenders_and_procurement: PM E‑DRIVE allocated ₹4,391 crore for 14,028 e‑buses; 13,800 e‑buses have been awarded to seven major cities, with tenders already concluded for 10,900 units (Roads Reimagined, 2026)
commercial_opportunities: EV charging infrastructure rollout – ₹2,000 crore earmarked for nationwide EVPCS, with ₹689 crore approved for 6,562 chargers across 3 oil‑marketing companies and 9 states (PM E‑DRIVE, 2026)
Battery‑cell manufacturing – private‑sector incentives under PLI‑ACC create opportunities for new plant development (PLI ACC, 2022)
risks: Policy continuity risk if future budgets reduce incentive levels
Supply‑chain bottlenecks in battery cell raw materials could constrain manufacturing expansion
